source_text: Following its unanimous adoption by acclamation at the Fourth International Symposium on Sexual Mutilations on August 11, 1996, the Ashley Montagu Resolution was positioned as a formal petition to the International Court of Justice (World Court) in The Hague, calling for a declaratory judgment that non-therapeutic genital mutilations of children violate core provisions of the United Nations Universal Declaration of Human Rights and the Convention on the Rights of the Child. [2]
